title: quarterly-bridge-all-hands-notes-may-04-2026
notes:
Quarterly Bridge All-Hands — Notes (May 4, 2026)

Purpose: short, cross-subteam sync to highlight riskiest customer-facing items and priorities for the quarter. Recorded for folks who couldn’t join live.

Attendees: ~120 eng + product viewers. Key leads: Ava Martinez (host), Liam Chen (serving runtime), Priya Kapoor (dedicated), Mateo Ruiz (private deployments), Sophie Wang (SRE), Rajesh Nair (product - hosted API).

Agenda:
- Quick wins & status highlights (5m)
- Risk flags and mitigations (10m)
- Customer/enterprise pilot updates (10m)
- Ops / oncall changes and pager review (5m)
- Q&A and parking lot (10m)

1) Quick highlights
- Serving runtime: merged continuous-batching improvements into canary; early tests show 12–18% tail-latency reduction for 32-token median workloads. Canaries in us-west are live for a subset of customers.
- Dedicated: first 50% of committed Dedicated pools are provisioned for Q2 beta customers; autoscaler defaults were updated to avoid aggressive cold-starts.
- Private: successful second run of the VPC install automation with ACME Bank pilot — zero config network policy applied end-to-end (notes in linked Confluence).
- Console/observability: token-level cost view now shows per-route breakdown (beta opt-in).

2) Risk flags and open mitigations
- KV cache regression (serving-runtime v2.3.1): discovered during canary that cross-session KV eviction caused rare hallucination regressions for long chat sessions. Rollback deliberate for impacted canaries; root cause narrowed to cache reindexing path under heavy multiplex. Mitigation plan: revert the aggressive reindexer (hotfix in review) and add a deterministic rehydration test. Owner: Liam Chen. Target: 2026-05-09.
- Dedicated capacity throughput variance: one tenant observed increased p99 generation time under bursty traffic patterns. We've scoped an autoscaler tuning and a new warm-pool feature to keep a small buffer of pre-warmed pods for 99th percentile. Owner: Priya Kapoor. ETA: 2026-05-18 for alpha.
- Private deployment discovery: small subset of customers hit TLS config drift in the customer-managed KMS path. Short-term suggestion: checklist and a verification script in the installer; long-term: stronger post-install auditing and a guided KMS wizard. Owner: Mateo Ruiz. ETA: verification script by 2026-05-14.

3) Customer & pilot updates
- ACME Bank (Private pilot): completed privacy-kms smoke tests; next step is perf tuning for long-context models (50k tokens). Working session scheduled 5/10.
- AtlasCommerce (Dedicated beta): migrated to reserved pools; reported 8% cost savings and stable latency after autoscaler adjustments.
- Two hosted API customers on canary saw improved throughput but the KV regression caused a small increase in content mutations — follow-up tickets created.

4) Ops / oncall changes
- SRE: introducing a secondary oncall (overnight) for Dedicated region ops during Q2 to reduce alert fatigue. Pilot team: Sophie Wang + rotation volunteers. Schedule and rotation sign-up in the team drive.
- Pager tuning: reducing noisy alerts by lowering sampling on minor request failures; increasing prominence of model variant fallback alerts.

5) Roadmap highlights & cross-team asks
- Serving runtime: prioritize deterministic KV test harness and add profiling hooks for quantized kernels. Request from product: provide a short doc describing expected performance delta per quantization profile by 5/20.
- Dedicated: collaborate with solutions-engineering to add a new deployment template for finance customers (compliance defaults). Solutions-eng to own template examples.
- Private: finalize the guided KMS wizard and include a diagnostic bundle uploader. Request for developer-experience: create a short onboarding walkthrough video for the installer (2–3 minutes).

6) Metrics snapshot (Q2 week 1)
- Mean token latency (hosted): 78ms -> target 70ms (work in progress).
- P99 latency (dedicated): 620ms -> target 500ms (autoscaler work).
- Platform error rate (5m window): 0.18% (baseline objective <0.2%).
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted, median): down 6% month-over-month thanks to batching optimizations.

7) Action items (owner — due)
- Liam Chen — land KV reindex revert + unit tests — 2026-05-09.
- Priya Kapoor — ship warm-pool alpha + autoscaler tuning doc — 2026-05-18.
- Mateo Ruiz — add TLS/KMS verification script to installer repo — 2026-05-14.
- Sophie Wang — finalize overnight secondary oncall schedule and rota — 2026-05-11.
- DevEx (assigned: Nisha) — onboarding video for private installer — 2026-05-21.

8) Q&A highlights
- Q: "Will rollback of KV reindex affect throughput?" A: Minimal impact expected; reindexer was CPU-heavy in rare paths. We will re-evaluate once we have more telemetry.
- Q: "Can customers opt into warm-pool?" A: Yes — will be configurable at pool-level in Dedicated; default off for early alpha.
- Q: "Installer will support air-gapped installs?" A: Yes — roadmap item; current pilot supports VPC w/ restricted egress, full air-gap plan in Q3.

9) Parking lot / follow-ups
- Request: canonical doc for model variant compatibility matrix across quantization levels (owner: runtime docs team).
- Follow-up: run a cross-team tabletop for a simulated Dedicated region outage — propose date 5/20.

Shoutouts / wins:
- Shoutout to the private deployments team for shipping the automated smoke test that caught the KMS drift.
- Thanks to the runtime perf folks for the batcher improvements — visible on alpha customers.

Notes and next all-hands cadence: We’ll do this Bridge-style sync monthly for Q2 and surface anything urgent via Slack #eng-all. Next bridge: June 1, 2026 (short agenda to be published 1 week prior).

Raw attachments & references: see linked_artifacts above and the following internal doc IDs: INF-ARCH-bridge-2026, JIRA INF-1234 (KV reindexer), PR github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/987.

If you find missing items or need a call to triage, ping Ava Martinez or open the ticket under INF-1234.

-- end of notes
